posts.caption:
A new bill filed in Austin would make it legal to keep a raccoon as a pet in Texas. You'd have to take an ownership course and get a yearly permit from Texas Parks and Wildlife. 
You also couldn't catch one in your backyard. It would have to come from a licensed breeder or wildlife rescuer. If it passes, it would take effect Sept. 1, 2027.

posts.caption:
Water levels at several North Texas lakes remain below normal following months of dry conditions, leaving large areas of previously submerged land exposed.

posts.caption:
Texans could soon pay less for Netflix, Hulu, Disney+ and more. Comptroller Don Huffines wants to end the state sales tax on streaming, saying lawmakers never voted for it.

Dallas has been ranked the best city in America to celebrate Thanksgiving in 2026, according to a new study by WalletHub.

posts.caption:
The Pentagon has failed its annual financial audit for the ninth straight year, according to a new report released Monday.
The Department of Defense has never passed a full financial audit since the process began in 2018, citing outdated accounting systems and financial management issues.
Despite the overall failure, officials reported progress, with 14 of 25 reporting entities passing their individual audits this year.
posts.media_description: x_screenshot: The Pentagon fails its financial audit for the 9th consecutive year
posts.headline_on_card: The Pentagon fails its financial audit for the 9th consecutive year

A Texas lawmaker wants to make English the official language of Texas.

Post Malone took to Instagram to vent after another frustrating Cowboys loss, saying there's no excuse for losing a game when Dak Prescott throws five touchdowns, only for the defense to give up nearly 600 yards.

notes: SCOPE: 120 most recent posts in the feed, Nov 13 7:02 PM to Nov 18 8:27 PM CT (read Nov 18, 2026). Times come from Facebook's hover tooltip, shown in the browser's America/Chicago zone. Facebook's page feed lazy-loads and skipped posts on the first scroll; they were filled in on a second, slower pass, so the set should be complete, but a missed post is still possible. Counts are what Facebook showed (rounded: 1.9K -> 1900). Views are null because every post is a still image. first_comment is only filled where the feed preview showed the page's own comment; several captions say 'Video in comments' but the preview showed someone else's comment, so it is null there. No pinned post, no story highlights, and no 'official partner' line on any post (that line is only in the page intro). One extra feed unit for the 'bat bandits' post looked like an attached reel; it duplicated that post and was dropped. VOLUME: posts per day: Nov 18: 23, Nov 17: 21, Nov 16: 22, Nov 15: 29, Nov 14: 22, Nov 13: 3 (Nov 13 and 18 are partial). Full days run 21-29, about 24 a day. TIMING: busiest hours: 11am (13), 8am (13), 10am (10), 7am (10), 4pm (9), 9am (8). Output runs from about 5:45am to 10:30pm, heaviest 7-11am, with a second wave in the afternoon. During games they post live score updates every 15-45 minutes (Cowboys-49ers Nov 15: 9:24am preview, 3:56pm coin toss, 4:00 TD, 4:33 TD, 4:55 halftime, 6:30, 6:46 final, 7:02 streak stat, then next-day reaction posts). FORMAT: all 120 are media_type photo, and every one is the same x_screenshot card: their own X post (DTX TV logo, 'Dallas Texas TV @DallasTexasTV', a one-line headline, then a photo). About 18 cards add a circular inset photo, usually a person's face or a logo. The caption never repeats the card headline; it rewrites the story in fuller news-brief form. Location tag ('is in Texas / DFW Area, Texas / Dallas, Texas / AT&T Stadium') appears on 14 posts. Hashtags: none. Emoji: almost none (the 🔥 and 🦝 appear on cards, not in captions). CAPTION SHAPE (by line breaks): 38 single-block captions (one or two sentences), 66 with two short paragraphs, 16 with three or more. There are two house styles: (a) a wire-style lead sentence with no final period, then a second line of context (e.g. Waymo, Senate flips, Seager), and (b) a plain-English local style with short sentences and a closing 'what happens next' line, e.g. 'Lawmakers take it up when the session starts Jan. 12.', 'Hinojosa takes office Jan. 19.', 'Nvidia has not confirmed anything.' Headlines sometimes start with 'BREAKING:', 'VIDEO:' or 'Dream job alert:'. Sources are credited inline ('according to ESPN', 'WalletHub study', 'Downdetector', 'the Financial Times reports'), never with a 'via' line. ENGAGEMENT: average reactions 1251, median 650. Every post is the same media type, so the difference comes from topic. Topic averages (count, average, median reactions): texas_bills_politics 11/3798/2600; cowboys_sports 31/1052/901; gta6_gaming 8/1103/916; crime_police 12/598/349; outages 13/612/513; weather 6/2674/3200; prices_retail 11/1963/860. Top 10 by reactions: 9500 - New Texas bill filed would have insurance pay for wigs for breast cancer patients; 8700 - Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa says teachers deserve a pay raise and it’s a top priority; 7700 - New bill could allow Texans to legally own raccoons as pets; 7700 - Gas keeps falling in North Texas, some residents now seeing prices under $3 a gallon; 6400 - H-E-B surprises 10,000 Texas shoppers with $100 gift cards, giving away $1 million in one day; 4000 - Michael Irvin tells Dak Prescott: “If you want to change the Cowboys, do it on the field, not at the podium”; 4000 - New Texas bill filed would require public schools to have a nurse on every campus; 3700 - Dallas is experiencing one of its coldest days in months, with heavy rain and temperatures in the 40s; 3600 - Texas has beaten more ranked teams than any other college football program this season; 3500 - New Texas bill filed would get rid of property taxes. Pattern: new Texas bills and 'what this means for your wallet' posts (pet raccoons, wig coverage, teacher pay, gas prices, H-E-B gift cards, property tax) average about 3-4x the reactions of the much more frequent sports posts (topic averages above). Halftime and in-game score posts usually land at 100-300 reactions. Shares are highest on practical or news-you-can-use posts (raccoon bill 1.8K, gas prices 918, PTO hack 751, meteor shower 629).
